title: Comparative Roman Egyptian female model life table
tableLocator: Sonia Zakrzewski, Life Expectancy (2015), Table 1, printed page 3 / PDF page 5, after Bagnall and Frier (1994).
applicability: An exploratory proxy for this fictional life. The source is a model for females in later Roman Egypt, not measured mortality for a male born in Ptolemaic Alexandria in 66 BCE. No precise Alexandrian death rates are claimed.
conversion: For an interval of n complete years with conditional death probability q, annual p = 1 - (1 - q)^(1/n). This assumes constant annual risk within each source interval.

oldestAgeTail.conversion: The source's 95+ interval is open-ended with q=1. That is not an annual death probability. As an explicit tail assumption, use annual p=1-exp(-1/1.187), then impose a computational age cap of 100.

additionalAssumptions: The engine records deaths in completed years at the start of the sampled interval; age 0 means before the first birthday. The source's continuous within-year timing is not reproduced.
The chosen table's sex, period and geography do not match the fictional protagonist exactly. This is a disclosed historical comparison, not a validated individual prediction.
No health-score, career, wealth, war or illness multiplier is added to the all-cause table, avoiding invented cause-specific rates and double counting.
Origins, personal event selection, outcome weights, stat effects, marriage/parenthood opportunities and stage ages are authored game assumptions, not population estimates.
Conditional survival into adulthood permits a long life. Low life expectancy at birth does not mean that every adult dies in their twenties.
